FR-P2: partly built: the intake panel produces the question list (FR-A7); every requirement the analyst drafts keeps a state by rule (customer-confirmed, customer-endorsed, assumption, vendor-proposed) and its sources (the request, a question id or 'proposed'), and a source outside the business is not kept; open questions stay in the canon and the brief; at pilot and production the package waits for a person's approval (the plan gate, FR-P7); the cockpit shows the states, sources and question states; not built: no UI concept is produced before the build (kernel/design_road.py only fixes the product's look), SMEs and end users never test a concept (stage 6, FR-R1, tests a running release), the approval is the plan gate (business owner, product owner or developer) and is off at explore and demo unless the owner turns it on, and nothing measures whether the user flow is understood without guidance or shows that content came from the business beyond the provenance rule; it would take a concept artifact (screens and flows) drafted by a concept role, a concept-test card where SMEs and end users record what they could not follow, and a package card for the PM before the spec stage
FR-P3: partly built: a question put to a person is settled only by a named person, never by the factory, and a blocking one stops the translation into a spec until it is answered; not built: there is no translation report of what carried into the build brief and what was dropped: kernel/spec.py normalize drops the analyst's requirements beyond the maturity's limit, those without a statement or a criterion, criteria beyond three and sources outside the business, and records none of it, and nothing compares the brief's answers and assumptions with the requirements that carried them; open questions that are not blocking do not stop the spec, so at explore and demo (no plan gate) a requirement resting on an unanswered question is built as vendor-proposed without the process owner deciding it; it would take a carried and dropped report written beside spec.json and shown on the plan card, and a gate that holds the spec while any question a requirement rests on is open
FR-P6: not built: no benefit metric, baseline or target is recorded at stage 1 (the business perspective is only prompted to ask about the success metric and its baseline as a panel question, kernel/intake.py), nothing measures that metric after a release reaches production, and no rule opens a new need-and-decision round when it falls short; it would take a benefit record (metric, how it is measured, baseline, target, owner) kept with the need, a measurement step after promotion that reads the same metric, and a below-target result filed as a signal that becomes a concept card for the business owner
FR-Q1: not built: IT configures environments in the factory's paved_roads.json (kernel/roads.py, FR-A8 and FR-Q4), not as code in a shared repository folder: there is no environments/ folder, no pull request flow and no IT review of one, and the Azure road renders a Container App from the road's settings instead of reading IT's environment code; it would take a shared environments repository the kernel reads its roads from, IT's merge of a reviewed pull request as the road's approval, and the road card naming the merged revision
FR-Q3: partly built: an IT person's answer to the panel's IT and security question makes the requirement resting on it customer-confirmed and decided by that person, and its probe criteria run as probes against staging (the holdouts step) and production (operate.probe) like any other criterion; IT's road rules (region, TLS, egress, secret references) are checked against every Azure deploy package (FR-Q4); not built: there is no it-confirmed provenance (tools/contract_check.py knows customer-confirmed, customer-endorsed, vendor-proposed, assumption and withdrawn only), the contract keeps no persona, so an IT requirement cannot be told from a business one there, IT cannot file a requirement directly (an IT change becomes a road card, FR-Q2, not a contract requirement), and no dry-run check kind proves a rule against the environment itself (egress, TLS version, identity); it would take an it-confirmed tier in the contract schema and its checker, an intake path for IT's requirements, and a dry-run check kind that the road runs
